definitions.explanation: Seven of something counted with {個|こ}, the broadest of the object counters. Typically used for compact, self-contained things such as fruit, eggs, or boxes.

examples.japanese: りんごを{七個|ななこ}{買|か}った。
{箱|はこ}の{中|なか}にたまごが{七個|ななこ}{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: There are seven eggs left in the box.

examples.japanese: {一人|ひとり}{三個|さんこ}ずつだと、{七個|ななこ}では{足|た}りない。
examples.english: At three each per person, seven isn't enough.

examples.japanese: {注文|ちゅうもん}したのは{八個|はっこ}だったはずだが、{届|とど}いたのは{七個|ななこ}だけだった。
examples.english: I was sure I ordered eight, but only seven arrived.

notes:
{七|なな} + the counter {個|こ}. The reading is ななこ; しちこ is not used.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {七個|ななこ}{入|い}り: a pack of seven
- {七個|ななこ}ずつ: seven each
- {七個|ななこ}{目|め}: the seventh one

NOTE ON THE SERIES: the 〜{個|こ} counter is regular except for {一個|いっこ}, {六個|ろっこ}, {八個|はっこ}, and {十個|じゅっこ}, which take small-tsu sound changes. {七個|ななこ} keeps the plain reading.
